The discussion is highly speculative and is necessarily limited in scope since there are no plans at this time for such a facility. For the purposes of analysis, it is assumed that the plant site would be located adjacent to the Tracts, probably in Sarpy Valley. The nature of the facility probably would be coal gasification, although for the most part impacts may be generalized to apply to any type of conversion facility. Air Quality
Major pollutants emitted from a power generation plant would be particulates, sulfur oxides and nitrogen oxides. From a gasification plant, major emissions probably would consist of hydrocarbons, with particulates, sulfur oxides and nitrogen oxides originating from onsite stream generation. Either process would result in water vapor losses due to cooling requirements. This analysis is drawn largely from Dames and Moore (1976).
During operation of a gasification facility, possible meteorological and air quality impacts would result from water vapor emitted from the cooling towers and stack emissions. If wet cooling towers are used, it can be expected that during periods of high humidity a vapor plume from the cooling towers would be visible. Typical coal gasification plants have relatively low cooling water losses; this coupled with the generally low relative humidity and the generally good ventilation associated with the Project Area suggests that the cooling tower impacts including fogging and icing would be minimal.
